title: Astronauts 'Save the Video Dish' in Spacewalk Repair
summary:
Imagine you're floating in space, 250 miles above Earth, trying to fix a giant TV dish. That's exactly what two astronauts did on Tuesday, August 25!

Anil Menon from NASA and Sophie Adenot from the European Space Agency spent 6.5 hours outside the International Space Station (ISS). Their mission: replace a broken antenna that helps send videos and messages to Earth.

The antenna stopped working last November. It couldn't track the satellites that bounce signals to Earth. That's a big deal—without it, astronauts can't video-call their families or send important data. Luckily, there was a spare antenna on the station, and a second one was still working.

Menon rode at the end of a giant robotic arm called Canadarm2, while Adenot climbed along handrails to join him. Together, they grabbed the spare antenna, attached it to the station, and plugged it in. Then they moved the broken one to a storage spot.

When they finished, Mission Control in Houston sang a funny song: "You just saved the video dish, you just saved the video dish!" It's a parody of a 1979 hit called "Video Killed the Radio Star." Menon laughed and said, "Oh my god, it is hard to top that!"

This was Menon's third spacewalk and Adenot's second. Adenot made history as the first woman from France to do a spacewalk. The whole repair took exactly 6.5 hours—from 8:27 a.m. to 2:57 p.m. Eastern time.

Now the ISS has two working antennas again. That means astronauts can keep talking to Earth—and we can keep watching their amazing videos from space!
why_it_matters: Fixing things in space is important because astronauts depend on communication to stay safe and share what they learn with people back home.

background_read: The International Space Station is a giant science lab that flies about 250 miles above Earth, where astronauts live and work for months at a time.
NASA is the U.S. space agency, and the European Space Agency is its European partner; both send astronauts on missions together.
Spacewalks are dangerous, so astronauts practice in giant swimming pools on Earth before going outside in space.

WHAT: They replaced a broken antenna outside the International Space Station.
WHERE: About 250 miles above Earth, outside the ISS.
WHY: To keep astronauts able to send videos and messages to Earth.
